text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.24% today as oil prices pulled back on news that the G7 will release 100 million barrels of diesel reserves over the next four months to ease global fuel shortages. The stock had already weakened over the past two weeks (down 3.85%), and this reserve release announcement pressured crude lower—US oil is trading at $96.16 per barrel, well below the world price of $113.96, signaling weak American demand or ample supply.

The broader backdrop remains complicated for the energy sector. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East (U.S. military buildup, potential Iran strikes) and trade friction with India over Russian oil purchases create genuine supply-side risks, but they're being offset near-term by the G7's deliberate effort to cool prices by flooding markets with reserves. For a major oil producer like ConocoPhillips, lower prices directly squeeze profit margins regardless of the longer-term supply picture.
